$comment: SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0. Anchoring extension 0.2.0 (proposal), written against Core v1.3 rev. 11 and reference files 5.2.0, and portable verification 0.3.0. Binds only an implementation that says it uses this extension.
title: Anchoring verification report
description: What a verifier found for each independent timestamp and each checkpoint, as separate dimensions, each naming the source it was checked against, with the scope of its conclusion. There is deliberately no overall result: no assertion stands for another, and nothing here is a legal conclusion or a Conformance Level.

trust_policy_ref.description: The trust policy the verifier configured independently of the export and the attachment.

trust_policy.description: Whether the policy itself was accepted: one public key, one key reference, one holder, one role; one reference, one entry. A refused policy fails every dimension that relies on it. The same object as in a signatures report.

attachment_digest.description: SHA-256 of the attachment's bytes as received.

export_digest.description: SHA-256 of the export's bytes as received.

chain_id.description: The chain the verifier checked, from its own configuration.

timestamp_count.description: The number of timestamps in the attachment. The report has one result for each, and each timestamp_index from 0 to this count minus 1 appears once. JSON Schema cannot compare two documents: a reader holding both checks it.

checkpoint_count.description: The number of checkpoints the verifier obtained or tried to obtain, each with one result.

then.description: A refused policy: nothing is verified against it.

ots_timestamp_result.description: An OpenTimestamps proof as one dimension. What a verified proof shows: the subject's bytes existed before the block it names was mined. It gives no time that holds: the header's time is the miner's statement, reported as miner_stated_time, never as existed_no_later_than; so no issuer's time is compared with it and no key state rests on it.

status.description: Verified only when every check below is.

proof.description: The proof read strictly: its magic and version, varints in their shortest form, within the limits, nothing after it.

subject_bytes.description: The subject's bytes are the seal, link or signature value it names, and the proof starts from their SHA-256.

operations.description: Every operation on the way is sha256, append or prepend.

attestation.description: A Bitcoin block header attestation is reached; a pending one only is unavailable.

header.description: The header of that block, from the verifier's source, holds the proof's result as its Merkle root, in the header's own byte order.

hash_hex.description: The block's hash, as explorers show it.

header_source_ref.description: The policy's source the header came from.

block.description: The block the proof leads to: what a verified proof shows.

miner_stated_time.description: The block header's time, as its miner states it. Consensus only holds it above the median of the previous eleven blocks; it is not a time the bytes existed by.

service_key_ref.description: The service key (role transparency_service) that signed the receipt, by its kid.

tree_size.description: The size of the log the receipt attests the statement in.

receipt.description: The service's receipt (RFC 9942) for a signed statement. verified means exactly: the service key named signed that this statement is in its log at tree_size. Not that the log is append-only, nor that it showed everyone the same log, nor when the statement was registered: a receipt states no time. unavailable: a receipt by a revoked service key, which cannot be shown made before the revocation, or no receipt held.

subject.description: The subject as the attachment states it, without its value.

status.description: The timestamp as one dimension: verified only when every check below allows it.

tsa_ref.description: The authority the token was checked against.

reference_source.description: Where the authority's certificate came from.

existed_no_later_than.description: genTime plus the token's accuracy, if it states one: the time T by which the bytes existed.

token.description: A TimeStampToken: CMS SignedData with one signer over a TSTInfo.

message_imprint.description: SHA-256, and the SHA-256 of the subject's bytes.

subject_bytes.description: The subject's bytes are the seal, link or signature value it names.

message_digest.description: The signed messageDigest is the SHA-256 of the encapsulated TSTInfo, and the signed content type is id-ct-TSTInfo.

tsa_signature.description: The signer the token names is the pinned certificate, and its signature over the signed attributes verifies with that certificate's key.

signer_certificate.description: The ESSCertIDv2 certificate hash, when the token has one made with SHA-256, is that of the pinned certificate. Without one, or with one made with another hash, not_checked.

tsa_state.description: genTime within the policy's window for the authority, and before its revocation.

else.description: No time is given for a timestamp that is not verified, and no issuer's time is compared with it.

issuer_time.description: The issuer's own time for the subject (a record's affirmation_record.timestamp, or a checkpoint's checkpoint_time) compared with existed_no_later_than. inconsistent: the issuer's time is later. It is reported apart from the timestamp, which it does not change.

obtained_from.description: configured_source: obtained by the verifier, outside the export, from a source its trust policy configures. same_export: found in the export, so never independent. beside_export: carried in the anchoring attachment beside the export, so never independent either; its prefix is reported on its own.

source_ref.description: The configured source it came from.

status.description: The checkpoint as an independent checkpoint: verified only when independence, signature and key_state are verified.

comparison.description: The export's entries against the checkpoint. Compared only with a verified checkpoint. Entries after count are not covered.

prefix.description: A checkpoint beside the export only: the export's first count entries against it, compared once its signature and key state are verified. Verified, it shows that those entries are the ones a witness the verifier trusts signed for, at the time time_basis names. It does not show that no later entry was dropped, that the issuer showed the same chain to everyone, or that the witness refused to sign another history.

time_basis.description: stated_time: the witness's checkpoint_time. independent_timestamp: a verified timestamp over the checkpoint's signature value.

attachment_index.description: A checkpoint beside the export only: its place in the attachment's checkpoints, counted from 0, so that a result is paired with its checkpoint without resting on the order of the results.

format.description: A checkpoint obtained as a SCITT signed statement (a transparency service with format scitt, or such a statement carried beside the export). Only it has receipt and log_consistency.

log_consistency.description: Whether the log is append-only and shown to everyone alike: not checked in this version. One inclusion proof shows neither; a consistency proof against a root the verifier holds would, and is not in this version.

freshness.description: A checkpoint beside the export only: always not_established, since the issuer chose which checkpoint to carry.

allOf.description: A SCITT signed statement (format scitt) has its receipt and log_consistency; nothing else has them.
From a transparency service, a statement is verified as an independent checkpoint only with its receipt verified: the service signed that it is in its log.

A checkpoint beside the export is never independent: its status and independence fail, it is not compared under comparison, and its prefix and freshness are reported. Only it has them, and only it may name its attachment_index.
A checkpoint found in the export is never independent.

key_state.description: The key's state when the signature was made. time_basis says what that time rests on: stated_time is the signer's own statement, never independent time; independent_timestamp is a verified timestamp over the signature value.

timestamp_index.description: The timestamp the time rests on.

allOf.description: After a compromise, only an independent timestamp earlier than revoked_at establishes the time.
